title: Business lines of credit
metaDescription: A business line of credit provides revolving access to capital for recurring cash-flow needs, seasonality, or short-term operating gaps. Learn when a line of credit commonly fits.
summary: The line-of-credit page explains when a revolving business facility can fit recurring operating needs better than a one-time loan.

hero.title: Business lines of credit for ongoing cash-flow flexibility.
hero.lead: A line of credit is designed for borrowing as needs arise rather than taking one lump sum once. Use this page to understand when revolving access to capital commonly fits day-to-day operations.

quickAnswer.definition: is a revolving credit facility that lets a business draw funds up to a limit, repay, and draw again as needed. It is commonly used for recurring or unpredictable operating needs such as cash-flow gaps, inventory cycles, or seasonality.

whoItFits.heading: When a line of credit tends to fit
items: Recurring cash-flow gaps rather than one large expense
Seasonal inventory or payroll timing needs
Working capital that may need to be drawn more than once
Businesses that value flexibility over a fixed lump-sum structure

whenItMayNotFit.heading: When a line of credit may not fit as well
items: A defined one-time project may be better served by a term loan or an SBA structure.
Long-term fixed-asset purchases such as owner-occupied property or heavy equipment may point more directly to SBA 504 or equipment-focused financing.

howFund44Fits.heading: How Fund44 fits

bullets: Clarifies the difference between revolving credit and a fixed term loan.

eligibilityCards.title: Revenue consistency
eligibilityCards.description: Because revolving credit supports ongoing operations, lenders commonly review consistent revenue and cash-flow patterns.

eligibilityCards.title: Use pattern
eligibilityCards.description: Lenders often want to understand whether the facility is meant for recurring working capital, seasonality, or another ongoing need.

eligibilityCards.title: Operating track record
eligibilityCards.description: Time in business and recent account performance can shape how a revolving facility is sized and underwritten.

sectionDisclosureHtml: Fund44 is not a lender. Line-of-credit eligibility, product availability, timelines, and terms are determined by third-party lenders and vary by provider and by business profile. This page is educational only.

ctaBanner.heading: Need flexibility for recurring operating needs?
ctaBanner.subheading: Preview whether a line of credit, a term loan, or another financing path better fits the way your business uses capital.

commonQuestions.question: How does a business line of credit work?
commonQuestions.answer: A line of credit lets a business draw funds up to an approved limit, repay, and draw again as needed. That structure can fit ongoing cash-flow needs better than taking one fixed lump sum.

commonQuestions.question: What is the difference between a line of credit and a term loan?
commonQuestions.answer: A line of credit is revolving and suits recurring needs, while a term loan provides a fixed amount up front for a defined project or purchase. The right fit depends on how often the business expects to borrow.

commonQuestions.question: What documents may be needed for a line of credit?
commonQuestions.answer: Common examples include bank statements, business financials, and revenue support. Exact documentation varies by lender and by the facility you are seeking.

commonQuestions.question: Does Fund44 issue business lines of credit?
commonQuestions.answer: No. Fund44 does not issue business lines of credit. Eligibility and terms are determined by third-party lenders.
